title: Source to sink 1 · sort → ORDER BY ${orderBy}
description: Follows every value that reaches `${orderBy}` in the ORDER BY clause of orderRepository.find (Semgrep node-postgres-sqli, src/repositories/orderRepository.js:8). userId and status are bound parameters ($1, $2) and are not traced.

cards.label: literal default, used when sort is absent
cards.title: SOURCE: 'created_at' default
description: **Source:** a string literal, used only when `filters.orderColumn` is falsy (no `sort` in the query, or `sort=`).
**Value here:** `'created_at'` for `GET /orders` (derived from code, not run).
**Next →** passed as the third argument of `find`, received as `orderBy` (step 7).

cards.label: user input, any logged-in user
cards.title: SOURCE: req.query.sort
description: **Source:** the `sort` query parameter of `GET /orders`. Express 5's default query parser gives a string, or an array when the key is repeated.
**Value here:** `sort = 'total'` for `GET /orders?status=open&sort=total` (example from docs/flows/list-orders.flow.json, not run).
**Who can send it:** any user with a valid API token (step 3); no role is required.
**Next →** checked? only `status` is (step 4); `sort` is passed on as `orderColumn` (step 5).

cards.label: auth only: any valid token can send sort
cards.title: Check on the path: requireAuth
description: **Control:** `requireAuth` requires a Bearer token found in `users.api_token`. It decides **who** can send `sort` (every authenticated user: alice, bob, admin), not **what** it contains. There is no `requireRole` on this route.
**Next →** the `status` allowlist (step 4).

cards.label: allowlist covers status, not sort
cards.title: Check on the path: status allowlist
description: **Gap:** the only validation in the controller checks `status` against `['open', 'shipped', 'cancelled']`. Nothing checks `sort`: no allowlist of columns, no type check, no length limit.
**Next →** `sort` is renamed `orderColumn` (step 5).

cards.title: sort → orderColumn
description: **Propagates:** `sort` is stored unchanged in `filters.orderColumn`.
**Value here:** `filters.orderColumn = 'total'` (derived from code, not run).
**Next →** read in `orderService.search` (step 6).

cards.title: orderColumn || 'created_at'
description: **Propagates:** a truthy `orderColumn` is passed through unchanged; only an empty value is replaced by the default (step 1). This is the merge point of paths A and B.
**Value here:** `'total'` (derived from code, not run).
**Next →** received by `find` as `orderBy` (step 7).

cards.title: orderColumn → orderBy
description: **Propagates:** the third argument is named `orderBy` in the repository. `find` has one caller (`orderService.search`).
**Value here:** `orderBy = 'total'`, or `'created_at'` from path B (derived from code, not run).
**Next →** interpolated into the SQL text (step 8).

cards.label: SQL text (ORDER BY)
cards.title: SINK: ORDER BY ${orderBy}
description: **Sink:** `orderBy` is written into the SQL text of `pool.query` with a template literal. `$1` and `$2` bind `userId` and `status`; identifiers such as an ORDER BY column cannot be bound, so the text is used as-is.
**Sink receives:** `... ORDER BY total` for `?sort=total`; `... ORDER BY created_at` with no `sort` (derived from code, not run).
**Path summary:** A: `req.query.sort` (user, any logged-in user) → no check on `sort` → `ORDER BY` text. B: literal `'created_at'` → `ORDER BY` text.
